title: Eel River Athapaskan peoples - Wikipedia
text: The Eel River Athapaskans include the Wailaki, Lassik, Nongatl, and Sinkyone (Sinkine) groups of Native Americans that traditionally live in present-day Mendocino, Trinity, and Humboldt counties on or near the Eel River and Van Duzen River of northwestern California.

title: Wailaki / Eel River Dene
text: Lassik was spoken on the lower reaches of Dobbyn Creek and south along the Eel River to Kekawaka Creek, with a large settlement at present-day Alderpoint, as well as at the headwaters of the North Fork Eel and Mad rivers. Wailaki was spoken in the territory around the Eel River south of Kekawaka Creek and along the North Fork of the Eel River (Elsasser 1978, Golla 2011).

title: The Athabaskan Language Family - Native American Netroots
text: November 21, 2019 - The California sub-family includes: Hoopa (Hupa), Cahto, Mattole (extinct), Nongatl, Sinkyone, Lassik, and Wailaki. In their book The Natural World of California Indians, Robert Heizer and Albert Elsassar divide the Athabaskan-speaking California tribes into two groups: the Hupa group (Hupa, Whilkut, Chilula) and the Southern Athabaskan group (Mattole, Nongatl, Sinkyone, Lassik, Wailaki, and Kato).
